rows.basis: Growth in gross 'Servers and networking equipment': 172,492m − 113,156m = 59,336m, against 131,819m of cash purchases of property and equipment. This counts all server and network growth, not only AI, and excludes construction in progress (+25,109m), land and buildings, and finance leases. The earnings release says the capex increase 'primarily reflects investments in artificial intelligence', which supports the reading but gives no share. The 84,772m of purchase commitments at year end is not split by AI.

Amazon guided to about $200bn of 2026 capex in February 2026 and raised it to about $220bn in the Q2 2026 release. Both figures cover the whole company, 'AI, chips, robotics, and low earth orbit satellites', so neither is the AI part. Releases during 2026 repeat that the increase 'primarily reflects investments in artificial intelligence', with no amount.
The FY2025 MD&A expects technology and infrastructure spending to increase 'including to support our artificial intelligence and machine learning initiatives'. It gives no amount or share.

The only AI revenue figure for FY2025 is Amazon Connect's $1bn annualized run rate (Q3 2025 release). That is a single product's run rate, not the year's AI revenue. AWS ($128,725m) is a cloud segment, not the AI line.

Q2 2026 release: AWS's AI business 'exceeded a $25 billion annual revenue run rate', growing by triple digits. This is a run rate at mid-2026, not fiscal-year revenue; FY2026 is not complete, and the pack has no revenue total to compute a share against.
